column1: # FILE-SET-RETIREMENTS.tsv -- the decision rows for scripts/check-rung-file-sets.py (TODO #358).
# That check reconciles every block of the delivery against the block it replaces and FAILS on a file,
# define, env var, option or whole block that the previous release carried and the new set does not
# (INVARIANTS.md, r331: block 00's ggml-alloc.c half went missing at the r328 re-base and shipped that
# way for two releases).  Restoring the content is the normal answer.  When the disappearance is
# DELIBERATE -- upstream absorbed the feature, a file was retired with a named replacement, a block was
# renumbered, a hunk moved to another block and no longer needs its old home -- record it here with a
# reason, in the same change, and say where it went.
# FORMAT, one row per line, TAB separated, `#` lines and blank lines ignored:
#     <from-release>
#   from-release   the tag of the release being replaced -- the `old` side the check printed.  `*` applies
#                  to any transition (use it only for a one-off local run, never in a commit).
#   block          a block number (`0000`, `0300`, `0100`) or `*` for any block.
#   kind           file | define | env | option | block
#   item           the path (`ggml/src/ggml-cuda/mmf.cu`), the macro (`GGML_GLU_INPLACE`), the env var
#                  (`GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_ROPE_SET_ROWS`), the long option (`--kv-window`), or the block
#                  number for `block`.
#   reason         one line: why it is gone, and where its content went.  Required.
# A ROW IS SCOPED TO ITS TRANSITION: it only applies while the check is comparing against the
# `from-release` it names, so a row can never suppress a later release's finding by coincidence.
# Prune rows for a transition once its WORKLOG.md entry records the decision -- the WORKLOG is the
# durable record, this file is the live ledger for the re-base in flight.  Rows that do not apply are
# counted in the check's summary ("N row(s) from another transition (not applied)"), never ignored
# silently.
